These files are derived from that change: the analyzer report and the sdk-output / sdk-vertical artifacts are all rendered from the fixtures' new locking scripts, and script-size-baseline.json is one row per fixture's byte length. RE-PIN 2026-09-17, W7 (56615a28) — Auction's locking script 1221 -> 1228 bytes. nLockTime is a spender-chosen NOT-BEFORE and cannot bound the chain from above, so `assert(extractLocktime(p) < this.deadline)` in `bid` was satisfiable by any late bidder writing a stale locktime; it is DELETED rather than repaired, because no guard makes `<` mean "now < T". `close` keeps `>= deadline` and gains `extractSequence(p) !== 0xffffffffn`, which is only sound because W1 made that decode unsigned — before W1 the same guard was the tautology #131 used to recommend.

That closed a live exploit, not just a doc lie: an all-final transaction takes nLockTime out of consensus scope, so the auctioneer could stamp `nLockTime = deadline` and close at height 1 before any bid arrived. Spend.validate() returned true before and false after, with the identical spend at nSequence 0xfffffffd still ACCEPTED — so the rejection is the sentinel itself and not a fee, size or binding difference. RE-PINNED by D26 (2026-11-18): Auction.close gains assert(extractLocktime(this.txPreimage) < 500000000n), the height-domain pin; the IR moves only by that assert. Independent evidence: conformance/witnesses/real-crypto/auction.json pins this file's new hash and adds a THEFT spend (close at nLockTime 500000000) that the real Spend refuses with the pin and accepted without it; all 7 tiers x 9 formats agree fold-OFF and fold-ON.

----- SECTION (2026-09-15, R-117 coordinate-canonicity gate on the EC value builtins) -----

R-117: a Point's WIDTH was gated by CL-BUG-095 (commit ea79620a); its two COORDINATES were never gated to be field elements. decomposePoint / cDecomposePoint BIN2NUM each half of the blob as an unsigned integer, so any width-fitting value is accepted -- x + p included, whenever x + p < 2^(8w). Field arithmetic downstream reduces mod p, so (x+p)||y behaves ARITHMETICALLY as the point (x, y), but affineAdd's two case selectors are bare OP_NUMEQUAL on the RAW decomposed values and do not reduce:  cond = (px == qx) AND (py == qy), notinf = NOT(px == qx AND NOT cond). For P and its alias both read 0, so the chord path runs on two equal points with den_chord = qx - px = 0 (mod p) and a Fermat inverse where inv(0) = 0.

REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION on @bsv/sdk's Spend with real secp256k1, before the fix, using the smallest-x secp256k1 point P = (1, 4218f20a...7e76a7ee) and P' = (1 + p, same y):
    ecAdd(P, P)   -> c7ffffff...4bb00d333   the correct 2P
    ecAdd(P, P')  -> fffffffe...81895441    x = p-2, i.e. -2x, and OFF CURVE
A script that SUCCEEDED and returned a blob that is not a point, for an input that denotes P + P. Both the R-052 doubling fix and the R-053 P + (-P) fix are driven by these same two selectors, so both are defeated by the same trick. The same reproduction runs on P-256 (x = 5) and P-384 (x = 2), where x + p likewise fits in the coordinate width.

THE FIX REJECTS RATHER THAN REDUCES. ecOnCurve / pNNNOnCurve already answer "no" to a non-canonical encoding (GAP-301 and its a = -3 twin), so reducing would leave the predicate and the value builtins disagreeing about whether the blob is a point at all. Rejecting keeps them aligned, and it is the policy CL-BUG-095 already set for the width: predicates clamp and flag, value producers OP_VERIFY. The gate is placed on the USER-FACING value builtins (ecAdd, ecMul, ecNegate and their P-256/P-384 twins) and deliberately NOT inside the shared decompose helper, because that helper is also on cEmitVerifyECDSA's path, where decompressPubKey and cEmitSigRangeGate have already decided -- with reasons recorded in their own docstrings -- that attacker-chosen bytes must make a total boolean builtin return false rather than abort the script. That placement is measurable, not asserted: p256-wallet, p384-wallet and r1-k1-wallet, which use only verifyECDSA_*, are byte-unchanged by this commit, while the ten-fixture EC sweep of R-052/R-053 moved them.

----- SECTION (2026-09-15, R-157 ecMul on-curve-or-infinity gate) -----

R-157: the ladder's correctness argument holds only for points ON the curve, every tier wrote that down, and nothing enforced it.

`ecMul(P, k)` does not compute k*P. It computes ((k mod n) + 3n)*P: the MSB-first ladder adds 3n so that a fixed high bit is always set, and +3n is a NO-OP ONLY WHEN ord(P) DIVIDES n. Cofactor 1 gives ord(P) = n for every point on the curve, so the trick is sound there and nowhere else. A point off the curve lies on some other curve y^2 = x^3 + b' whose order is unrelated to n, and the whole computation silently answers a different question.

REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION on @bsv/sdk's Spend, before the fix, with the off-curve point P = (5, 7), which lies on y^2 = x^3 - 76:
    ecMul(P, 1n)  ->  c8b039d1...9438f2ff   which is NOT P
    ecMul(P, 2n)  ->  e673c72b...c8dde4c8   which is NOT 2P
Both match ((k mod n) + 3n)*P computed off-chain on that other curve EXACTLY, which is how the mechanism was identified rather than guessed. `ecMul(P, 1n) != P` is the whole finding: the primitive violated its own contract for every off-curve input, not merely a contrived one.

The degenerate sub-case is worse. For a 2-torsion point of the other curve -- any (x, 0) -- every multiple collapses to the all-zero blob, measured for k = 1, 2, 3, 5, because the ladder's unguarded mixed-add hits H = R = 0 mid-ladder, sets Z3 = 0, and a Jacobian accumulator at infinity can never leave it. Combined with R-053 -- which correctly taught ecAdd that the all-zero blob is the identity -- that turns a Schnorr-shaped s*G == R + e*P verifier into a free pass: choose an off-curve P of order 2, e*P is O, R + O is R, and any s with R = s*G verifies with no knowledge of any discrete log. R-053 is right and is not being undone; this is the other half of the same seam.

WHY THE GATE BELONGS IN ecMul AND NOT IN THE CALLER. The +3n offset is INTERNAL to ecMul: a caller cannot see it, cannot know the obligation exists without reading the codegen, and gains nothing by checking what ecMul can check more cheaply (ecOnCurve is 816 bytes against ecMul's 428,754 -- 0.19%). The obligation WAS written down, in all seven tiers, in buildJacobianAddOrDoubleInline's own docstring: "callers who accept untrusted points must gate them on ecOnCurve first". Nothing enforced it, and the repository's own schnorr-zkp fixture takes its pubKey from a DEPLOYER-supplied constructor slot, where that idiom is not even reachable.

WHY NOT ecAdd, which is the other half of the boundary: affineAdd implements the group law with no n-dependent trick, so on an off-curve operand it returns the CORRECT sum on that operand's own curve -- it does not lie. And O, which is deliberately not on the curve, must keep flowing through ecAdd for R-053 to hold. Gating the adder would break a working primitive to fix a different one.

O IS EXEMPTED and the exemption is load-bearing: ecMul(P, 0n) returns the all-zero blob, ecAdd(P, -P) returns it, and the EC optimizer folds to it, so O is a reachable runtime operand -- while ecOnCurve(O) is false by construction (0^2 != 0^3 + b). A bare on-curve gate would reject the identity this codegen manufactures itself. The gate is therefore `onCurve(P) OR P == O`.

WIDENED from 4 vectors to 34, regenerated by tests/generate-vectors/bn254 against gnark-crypto. BN254/Groth16 ships Stack-IR codegen in the Go tier only, so cross-tier parity is definitionally vacuous for it and this file is the entire oracle for the pairing — the most security-critical operation in the Groth16 path. At 4 vectors it was also the ONLY file under tests/vectors/ with zero consumers: nothing in the repo read it, so those 4 vectors were never executed by any test. The new corpus is built to be falsifiable by ALGEBRA over the recorded values, which needs neither a second pairing implementation nor an upstream KAT (neither of which this repo has): 6 bilinearity classes, each holding every spelling of one scalar product a*b mod r (scalar on G1, scalar on G2, and each non-trivial factorisation, plus an (r+2) reduction case) and each required to carry one byte-identical expected_gt; 7 must-be-identity vectors including e(O, G2), e(G1, O) and the four-term Groth16 shape e(A,B)*e(-alpha,beta)*e(-C,delta)*e(-vk_x,gamma) = 1; and 4 negative controls that must NOT be the identity, so a verifier that returns 1 for everything is falsified too. INDEPENDENT CHECK, and this file’s first consumer: conformance/scripts/check-bn254-pairing-invariants.mjs enforces bilinearity, degeneracy, non-degeneracy, field-element canonicity (< p) and a coverage floor over the checked-in bytes; run 2026-08-17 on this exact content, all invariants hold, and its own --self-test shows all 8 scenarios rejecting/passing as expected. REPRODUCIBILITY: tests/generate-vectors/verify-reproducible.sh re-runs every generator and diffs; on this tree all 22 vector files reproduce byte-for-byte, so the pinned bytes are what gnark-crypto and Plonky3 actually emit rather than a recorded claim.

Scripts shrank slightly (the PICKed key-pair address is cheaper than a 4-byte push); expected-ir.json did not move, because the change is confined to stack lowering. All 7 tiers emit byte-identical hex for this fixture (conformance 72/72 in both fold modes). Both fixes were RED-proved: reverting either one individually turns that on-chain accept test red. F-038 / R34 (user decision 2026-10-04): expected-ir.json gains one top-level key parentClass (value = the contract's base class, checked against TS parse for all 85 fixtures); dispatcher verified the diff is exactly +1 line and no expected-script.hex moved; all 7 tiers agree (golden 85/85, --ir-parity 85, --ir-roundtrip 85) || PREVIOUS: NEW-014: `&&` / `||` now SHORT-CIRCUIT on-chain. They lowered to OP_BOOLAND / OP_BOOLOR, which are binary stack ops -- both operands must already be ON the stack, so both were evaluated unconditionally. spec/semantics.md 3.7 licensed that with "This is safe in Runar because all expressions are pure (no side effects beyond assert)", but purity is not TOTALITY: 10 of the same document lists division by zero as a runtime failure, and OP_SPLIT / OP_NUM2BIN abort out of range. Evaluating the operand the source skipped therefore ABORTED the script, so the ordinary defensive guard `assert(d === 0n || (100n / d) > 1n)` compiled to a locking script the chain rejects for exactly the input the guard exists to protect -- a permanently unspendable UTXO -- while the AST interpreter (which short-circuits) reported success. `&&` / `||` now desugar to the ternary, which stack lowering already emits as real OP_IF / OP_ELSE control flow (3.9 already specified the untaken arm as unevaluated), so the moved bytes are OP_BOOLAND/OP_BOOLOR (0x9a/0x9b) becoming OP_IF/OP_ELSE/OP_ENDIF (0x63/0x67/0x68). EVIDENCE IS THE DIFFERENTIAL ORACLE, NOT A SELF-GOLDEN: the OLD bytes are REJECTED by @bsv/sdk's real Spend.validate() on inputs the source accepts. The three specific consensus rejections pinned in packages/runar-testing/src/__tests__/shortcircuit-consensus-vm.test.ts are "OP_DIV cannot divide by zero!" (d=0 through a `||` zero-guard), "OP_SPLIT requires the first stack item to be a non-negative number less than or equal to the size of the second-from-top stack item" (a guarded out-of-range substr), and "OP_NUM2BIN requires that the size expressed in the top stack item is large enough to hold the value expressed in the second-from-top stack item" (a guarded undersized num2bin). That suite pins BOTH directions for every short-circuiting case -- the input that must not reach the right operand, the input that must reach it and hold, and the input that must reach it and reject -- so a compiler that simply dropped the right operand could not pass it. All 7 tiers emit byte-identical hex and IR for this fixture in both fold modes (conformance 72/72), and the regeneration moved ONLY the six files of the three fixtures whose sources use `&&` / `||`; a control regeneration on the unpatched tree was a byte-for-byte no-op, so every moved byte is attributable to this change alone. THIS FILE: the ANF IR (the desugar happens in ANF lowering, so the IR moves too) for fixture `boolean-logic`, whose source examples/ts/boolean-logic/BooleanLogic.runar.ts uses both `&&` and `||`, including a nested `bothAbove || (eitherAbove && notFlag)`. Its bytes move because those operators change lowering; no other behaviour of the fixture changed.

----- SECTION (2026-09-15, R-157 ecMul on-curve-or-infinity gate) -----

R-157: the ladder's correctness argument holds only for points ON the curve, every tier wrote that down, and nothing enforced it.

`ecMul(P, k)` does not compute k*P. It computes ((k mod n) + 3n)*P: the MSB-first ladder adds 3n so that a fixed high bit is always set, and +3n is a NO-OP ONLY WHEN ord(P) DIVIDES n. Cofactor 1 gives ord(P) = n for every point on the curve, so the trick is sound there and nowhere else. A point off the curve lies on some other curve y^2 = x^3 + b' whose order is unrelated to n, and the whole computation silently answers a different question.

REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION on @bsv/sdk's Spend, before the fix, with the off-curve point P = (5, 7), which lies on y^2 = x^3 - 76:
    ecMul(P, 1n)  ->  c8b039d1...9438f2ff   which is NOT P
    ecMul(P, 2n)  ->  e673c72b...c8dde4c8   which is NOT 2P
Both match ((k mod n) + 3n)*P computed off-chain on that other curve EXACTLY, which is how the mechanism was identified rather than guessed. `ecMul(P, 1n) != P` is the whole finding: the primitive violated its own contract for every off-curve input, not merely a contrived one.

The degenerate sub-case is worse. For a 2-torsion point of the other curve -- any (x, 0) -- every multiple collapses to the all-zero blob, measured for k = 1, 2, 3, 5, because the ladder's unguarded mixed-add hits H = R = 0 mid-ladder, sets Z3 = 0, and a Jacobian accumulator at infinity can never leave it. Combined with R-053 -- which correctly taught ecAdd that the all-zero blob is the identity -- that turns a Schnorr-shaped s*G == R + e*P verifier into a free pass: choose an off-curve P of order 2, e*P is O, R + O is R, and any s with R = s*G verifies with no knowledge of any discrete log. R-053 is right and is not being undone; this is the other half of the same seam.

WHY THE GATE BELONGS IN ecMul AND NOT IN THE CALLER. The +3n offset is INTERNAL to ecMul: a caller cannot see it, cannot know the obligation exists without reading the codegen, and gains nothing by checking what ecMul can check more cheaply (ecOnCurve is 816 bytes against ecMul's 428,754 -- 0.19%). The obligation WAS written down, in all seven tiers, in buildJacobianAddOrDoubleInline's own docstring: "callers who accept untrusted points must gate them on ecOnCurve first". Nothing enforced it, and the repository's own schnorr-zkp fixture takes its pubKey from a DEPLOYER-supplied constructor slot, where that idiom is not even reachable.

WHY NOT ecAdd, which is the other half of the boundary: affineAdd implements the group law with no n-dependent trick, so on an off-curve operand it returns the CORRECT sum on that operand's own curve -- it does not lie. And O, which is deliberately not on the curve, must keep flowing through ecAdd for R-053 to hold. Gating the adder would break a working primitive to fix a different one.

O IS EXEMPTED and the exemption is load-bearing: ecMul(P, 0n) returns the all-zero blob, ecAdd(P, -P) returns it, and the EC optimizer folds to it, so O is a reachable runtime operand -- while ecOnCurve(O) is false by construction (0^2 != 0^3 + b). A bare on-curve gate would reject the identity this codegen manufactures itself. The gate is therefore `onCurve(P) OR P == O`.

The gate follows that SLH-DSA prologue convention exactly (OP_SIZE / push / OP_EQUALVERIFY, hard failure rather than a false result), which is consistent with the primitive already aborting on a short signature. Content: 42 mappings. opcode 0 (let sum = 0) -> 11:8; the five iteration-variable pushes, opcodes 1/9/17/25/33 (OP_0..OP_4), -> 12:8 (loop header); the other 34 loop opcodes (OP_2 OP_PICK OP_ROT OP_SWAP OP_ADD OP_SWAP OP_ADD per iteration, plus the final iteration's ROT/ROT pair) -> 13:12 (sum = sum + start + i); opcodes 40-41 (the assert) -> 15:8. At HEAD the same 42 mappings existed with identical opcodeIndex values and opcodes 2-8, 10-16, 18-24, 26-32, 34-39 on the loop header line instead, so the delta the pin authorizes vs the pre-fix output is exactly those 34 entries' line/column. Verified against: (1) the independent source-anchor oracle (conformance/source-map/run.ts checkSourceAnchors, which re-reads each claimed line/column from the real source file): byte-id/structural/anchor OK for bounded-loop in all 7 tiers; (2) a second (and third..seventh) implementation: all seven tiers produce the same opcodeIndex set and the same header/body/pre/post partition of it, opcode for opcode (each tier compiles its own surface, so absolute lines/columns differ by design), and each tier has its own red-then-green test asserting this map; (3) script hex unchanged (conformance golden STRICT and --multi-format bounded-loop in both fold modes), since source locations never reach the bytes.

PR F (D11): sha256Finalize is now modelled in every SDK ANF interpreter (TS SDK, Go, Python, Ruby, Rust, Zig, Java), which previously returned null/'0n' or refused the builtin. These strict-mode goldens were stamped from the TS reference interpreter and checked against two independent oracles: (1) the lenient-mode goldens for the same cases, whose digests were computed with Python hashlib (and runar-py's builtin for 2^63+24), and (2) the compiled script on the real @bsv/sdk Spend, which agrees. New files; no existing golden moved.

PR G (D16): sha256Compress is now modelled in every SDK ANF interpreter (TS SDK, Go, Python, Ruby, Rust, Zig, Java), which previously returned nil/None/undefined or refused the builtin. These strict-mode goldens equal the lenient goldens for the same cases, whose digests were computed independently with a pure-Python FIPS 180-4 compression that was itself checked against Python hashlib (sha256-compress-abc = SHA-256('abc'); sha256-compress-chained = SHA-256 of the 56-byte two-block FIPS vector, compressing its second block from the first block's state; sha256-compress-arbitrary-state from the same reference on a non-IV state), and against the compiled script on the real @bsv/sdk Spend (the script-semantics oracle in cross-interpreter.test.ts), which agrees. All seven interpreters reproduce each golden byte-for-byte in conformance/anf-interpreter/cross-interpreter-strict.test.ts, and conformance/anf-interpreter/sha256-compress-domain.test.ts replays every row of conformance/witnesses/real-crypto/sha256-compress.json (including the F-114 state / block size refusals) through all seven. New files; no existing golden moved.

#197 (add-output-env): addOutput(sats, ...values) serialises its values into its own output and does NOT write the property that a later load_prop reads; only update_prop does. Every SDK ANF interpreter (TS, Go, Rust, Python, Ruby, Zig, Java) wrote the property env on add_output, so a second addOutput(.., this.count + 100n) read the first output's value and the continuation it built was rejected by the covenant. New file; no existing golden moved. This case (fan-out) pins last-write state count=100n. Independent evidence: conformance/anf-interpreter/add-output-env.test.ts compiles programs/AddOutputEnv.runar.ts, deploys it and calls the method through the validating MockProvider, which replays the broadcast on the real @bsv/sdk Spend (OP_PUSH_TX + the covenant's own hashOutputs reconstruction, so an output that differs by one byte is refused), then decodes the continuation states off the broadcast outputs (byte layout, not by re-running the transition): fanOut commits count+1 and count+100, bumpBetween commits count+1 and (count+5)+100; the golden state equals the LAST on-chain continuation. All seven interpreters reproduce the golden byte-for-byte in cross-interpreter-strict.test.ts; before the fix the six non-TS tiers returned 101 / 106 (RED).

D12 BM-F1 (bin2num-sign-byte): bin2num of 0xff00 into a state field must yield 255, as OP_BIN2NUM reads the sign from the LAST byte (here a 0x00 padding byte). The Zig SDK interpreter stripped the padding before reading the sign and derived the wrong value, so its continuation was refused. New file; no existing golden moved. Independent evidence: cross-interpreter.test.ts's script oracle deploys the source and spends it on the real @bsv/sdk Spend, checking the pinned state against the continuation the covenant accepts; all seven ANF drivers reproduce this golden in cross-interpreter-strict.test.ts (RUNAR_ANF_DRIVERS_STRICT=1, 557/557).
